In fact, from his Thesis until his generalized proof of Riemann-Roch, passing through the creation of abelian categories, Grothendieck detected ubiq- uitous appearances of projectivity and injectivity in many mathematical regions: projective and injective products (Thesis [1949-53]), projective and injective norms (Résumé [1953c]), existence of enough injectives in abelian categories with a generator and infinitude axioms in order to reconstruct homology from derived functors (Tôhoku [1955-56]), inductive sub-specializations (= “spatial- izations”) of the generalized Riemann-Roch proof in the projective and injective cases (Rapport Riemann-Roch [1955-57]).
